title: THE FIRE THAT NEVER WENT OUT

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "The LORD said to Moses: 'Give Aaron and his sons this command: "These are the regulations for the burnt offering: The burnt offering is to remain on the altar hearth throughout the night, till morning, and the fire must be kept burning on the altar."'" - Lev 6:8-9 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Through the night, till morning, the fire kept burning.

Israel slept. The camp was dark. Nobody was watching, nobody was worshipping, nobody was bringing anything. And on the altar, the offering continued to burn.

There is a picture here worth carrying with you. The atonement did not depend on Israel's attention. It burned while they were unconscious.

Many believers feel their standing with God rises and falls with their spiritual performance — strong after a good quiet time, distant after a distracted week. But the fire on the altar was not fed by the worshippers' alertness. It burned because God commanded it to burn.

Christ's finished work does not flicker when your devotion does. He remains faithful, for he cannot disown himself (2 Tim 2:13). Nothing can separate us from the love of God that is in Christ Jesus our Lord (Rom 8:38-39) — not even our own dry seasons.

You will have nights when you have nothing to bring. You will have weeks when prayer feels mechanical. The altar is still burning. Your acceptance was never being sustained by you.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Does my sense of God's acceptance rise and fall with my spiritual performance?
2. What would change if I rested in a work that continues even when I am not attending to it?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You that the fire of Christ's finished work does not go out when I grow tired. Steady my heart on what You have done, not on how I feel. Amen.
